body:
Quick mode — no voting panel. Rounds 1-3: up to 6 Cursor specialists in parallel (plan-fidelity when plan available) + generic Codex. Main agent reviewed findings across up to 3 rounds.

Round 1: 5 Cursor specialists (OK) + 1 Codex generic (OK) + 1 Cursor security (NOT_SUBSTANTIVE).
Accepted: 2 findings (move explanatory text before directive, update NEVER #7 exception).
Rejected: 4 findings (larch-logs expected pattern, nits about wording).

## Rejected Code Review Findings
### [Code Review] All Reviewers (round 1)
**Finding**: larch-logs/implement/D759CBC1-.../manifest.json and sibling files committed to the branch with status: "in-progress" and local absolute paths.
**Reason not implemented**: This is the repo's established larch-log flush pattern — main already has identical chore(larch-logs) commits from prior runs (e.g., 20c6d25, e1bb125). The manifest records operator_cwd and operator_repo_root as local paths by design; prior merged PRs contain the same fields. The pre-bump flush at Step 7a always commits in-progress state; the final larch-log update after merge changes status to "done". Not a regression.

### [Code Review] Edge-cases Cursor (round 1)
**Finding**: In NEVER #12, "Both terminal patterns are inputs to the wrapper" overstates the mechanical contract; post-design-boundary.sh parses manifest files, not trailing /design lines.
**Reason not implemented**: The sentence uses "inputs" in the prose/orchestrator sense — both patterns signal to the orchestrator that the wrapper must be called next — not as arguments parsed by the script. The wording is accurate at the prose level and no scripts parse the trailing lines.

### [Code Review] Correctness Cursor (round 1) / Plan-fidelity Cursor (round 1)
**Finding**: "How to apply" in NEVER #12 should explicitly name the exact observable symptom.
**Reason not implemented**: The "Why" section already names the exact symptom: "the exact observable symptom this rule targets is a turn that ends immediately after /design returns ... instead of invoking the mandatory post-design-boundary wrapper as the next action." The "How to apply" stays procedural (what to do), while "Why" names the symptom. This aligns with the rule's structure and the issue's request.

### [Code Review] Edge-cases Cursor (round 1)
**Finding**: Add "no output after this line" clause to prevent trailing output after the directive.
**Reason not implemented**: The instruction uses "final output line" which already establishes the constraint. The "Do NOT write any farewell message" sentence preceding it provides the behavioral guardrail. An additional "no output after this line" clause would be redundant.
